nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green product design|Life cycle assessment integration_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: What are the seven input parameters taken into account by the model for life cycle assessment in garment production?
nodes.answer: The model takes into account seven input parameters from the life cycle stages of production, supply chain, and use, including garment design options, fibre content options, and seasonal variations between winter and all seasons.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green product design|Life cycle assessment integration_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: Which phase of Life Cycle Inventory development primarily integrates digital technologies according to the study?
nodes.answer: Digital technologies are primarily integrated in the Life Cycle Inventory phase, focusing on capturing closing and narrowing loops.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green product design|Life cycle assessment integration_qna_002
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How can combining different digital technologies benefit environmental assessments in LCA?
nodes.answer: Combining different digital technologies may significantly improve the reliability and accuracy of environmental assessments at different stages of LCA.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green product design|Life cycle assessment integration_qna_003
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How can the lack of standardization affect the integration of digital technologies into LCA?
nodes.answer: The lack of standardization can complicate data integration and hinder the effectiveness of assessments.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green product design|Life cycle assessment integration_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some of the challenges and opportunities associated with integrating environment and nutrition in the life cycle assessment of food items, as discussed in the FAO report by McLaren, A. Beardy, A. Henderson, et al.?
nodes.answer: The FAO report by McLaren, A. Beardy, A. Henderson, et al. highlights the opportunities and challenges in integrating environment and nutrition in the life cycle assessment of food items, providing insights into this complex relationship for further exploration.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Green product design|Life cycle assessment integration_qna_006
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the significance of estimating embodied global energy and air-emission intensities of products for building a Japanese input-output life cycle assessment database?
nodes.answer: Estimating embodied global energy and air-emission intensities helps in understanding the environmental impact of Japanese products, which is crucial for developing sustainable policies and practices.
